records.title: Underway after fueling; navigational passage

fields.event: Underway in accordance with CTG 72.4 Routing Order 1-43 having received 15,900 gallons of fuel from USS COUCAL. It was found we had been set considerable to westward while lying to refueling. The night was dark and islands difficult to see. At 0200 cleared the ARCHIPELAGO, passing between CONFLICT GROUP and LUNN Island, instead of between LUNN Island and TORLESSE Island as had been original intention. Navigated with caution, using SJ, fathometer, and echo ranging on reefs.

records.title: Attack 1

fields.form:
U.S.S. SILVERSIDES
(H) ATTACK DATA
TORPEDO ATTACK No. 1
PATROL NO. 6
LAT 4-36 N.
LONG 149-20 E
TIME 0750 K.  DATE August 2, 1943
TARGET DATA
DESCRIPTION
Contact was made with the target visually as it emerged from
a squally background, shortly after sunrise.  Sea was calm,
sky almost completely overcast, frequent heavy rain squalls.
Range was closing rapidly, from appearance masts angle on
the bow was nearly zero, submerged before he sighted us and
commenced approach.  Target was later identified as similar
to KAIKWA MARU (ONI 14 P.63) and probably was converted
to an AV as it had only three goalposts instead of four, and
closely resembled the picture shown of the converted AV.
-24-
fields.torpedoes:
U.S.S. SILVERSIDES - Report of Sixth War Patrol.
TARGET DATA (Cont.)
Closed track at 9 kts. on normal approach course.  While
standing by to fire, target zigged away, making track 150
instead of 90.  Changed setup and commenced firing, using 9
sec. interval and a speed spread of 13 to 16 kts.  First two
torpedoes were prematures, target sighted these and avoided
other two torpedoes.  Target then commenced shooting 5" gun
in our general direction, dropped a "nuisance" depth charge
and headed away from us.  Surfaced with him in sight and
started chase and end around run at full speed.  Target
ducked into a heavy rain squall and contact was not regained.
We searched for him until dusk.  Weather squally all day.
SHIPS SUNK
NONE
SHIPS DAMAGED NONE
DAMAGE DETERMINED BY: Saw no damage.
TARGET DRAFT 15 ft. Course 270, speed 14, range 2200-2320.

Had him in a fair position, range 2400, angle on bow 70 stbd, gyro angle 350 coming on to zero.

Raised periscope to put in firing bearing; target had zigged away angle on bow now 130 stbd. Decided to accept change of track and go ahead and shoot.

Fired four bow tubes, 9 sec. firing interval, using speed spread of 13 to 16 kts. First two torpedoes fired were definitely prematures. Target saw these and maneuvered to port, evading last two torpedoes. Target then dropped a depth charge and opened fire with his deck gun at the periscope.

DESCRIPTION
At 0547 sighted masts of target bearing 021 T,
estimated target course 170 T.  Increased speed to 19 kts
and worked into position dead ahead of target, keeping his
masts in sight.  It was clear and sunny, sea almost a flat
calm.  At 0900 having worked into position ahead, submerged
and started approach.  Set torpedoes at 15 feet.  At 0918

possible hit.  Later identified ship as H.I.J.M.S. TAIGEI
class, ONI 14 P. 177).  He turned toward to ram, went deep
and he dropped five depth charges about a minute apart, the
first one exploding as we passed 180 feet, none of them were
close.

fields.narrative:
Had masts bearing 350 T, submerged on course 170 T.

Sighted masts through periscope, angle on the bow zero. By 0934 his angle on the bow was still zero, range decreasing rapidly, from bow on appeared to be a destroyer. Ordered stern tubes set at 8 feet. Believed he might be running ahead of a more valuable target I could not see, so c/c to 100 T to open out on track and better identify him. Went to battle stations. Set torpedo depth at 15 feet. By 0940 his angle on bow was 15° port, range 3200 yds, speed checking 18 kts. Still looked like a destroyer or destroyer leader. By 0944 his angle on bow was 30° port, indicating zig to 184 T, apparently not a destroyer, but had a long flat deck between his two masts and a single stack amidships. Sea was glassy calm, periscope exposures of necessity brief. Standing by to fire four stern tubes.

0947-00 Fired # 7 tube. 0947-08 Fired # 8 tube. 0947-15 Heard explosion, premature # 7. 0947-22 Fired # 9 tube. 0947-30 Fired # 10 tube. 0947-38 Heard and saw explosion, premature # 9 torpedo. 0948-33 Saw explosion about amidships near the target, but it had appearance of exploding between target and submarine. First impression was that he was throwing a depth charge at us (or toward premature) with a side thrower, but this may well have been a hit with # 10 torpedo. At this time his angle on bow was about 90 P and he took up entire field in periscope in high power. From his appearance later identified him as a submarine tender, TAIGEI class. Sound could only hear one torpedo running, which further indicates # 10 was a possible hit.

fields.event: He was swinging rapidly toward us, so 0950 Ordered 300 feet, rigged for depth charge. 0951 First depth charge, passing 180 feet. 0952 Second depth charge. 0952-30 Third depth charge. 0953 Fourth depth charge. 0955 Fifth depth charge. While the charges all sounded heavy, none could be described as "close", and all appeared to be on starboard quarter. 0955-1020 Maneuvered to keep screws astern. He would stop occasionally, but appeared to have lost us and did not drop any more. Bathythermograph indicated a layer at 175 feet, which we were well below. He did not echo range. 1020 Soundman heard cracking noises, which he attributed to target breaking up. However considering aggressive actions of target after firing, this is seriously doubted. It is believed that there was a possibility of one hit in the target. Screws were no longer heard.

fields.form:
U.S.S. SILVERSIDES                   PATROL NO. 6
TORPEDO ATTACK No. 3
TIME 0107 K DATE August 30, 1943.   LAT 0240 N.  LONG 150-00 E
TARGET DATA
DESCRIPTION
Original contact with target made at 1012 K
the previous day and had been stalking and tracking target
continuously since that time.  One day submerged and one
night submerged approach had been made previously but no
torpedoes fired as was not in favorable firing position.
At 0043, K, with target bearing 043 T, range 11,500 yds,
started surface approach.  Radar working well, two escorts
picked up at about 6000 yds, one on port bow, one on star-
board quarter.  Came in on a 50 starboard track, maintaining
a small silhouette and using slow speed to reduce wake.  Radar
ranges and TBT bearings were introduced into TDC about every
30 sec during approach and TDC was checking with plot.  At
0106 it appeared that we would not be able to sneak in much
further undetected so fired a spread of six torpedoes, using
a speed spread of 7.5 kts.  Fired six torpedoes at this target
because it was southbound, loaded and if previous rate of
prematures was maintained only three would cross the track.
Used depth setting of 18 feet to minimize chance of prematures.
No prematures were obtained and the tracks of three of the
torpedoes appeared to pass under the target.  It is believed
that he had a shallow draft and depth setting was too deep.
After attack, retired on the surface at 18 kts.

fields.narrative:
With target bearing 048 T, range 11,500 yds, started approach. There were now a few more clouds and it was difficult to see target through binoculars at ranges in excess of 6000 yds. Radar did not pick up escorts until their ranges were about 6000 yds, at which time one escort was located on target port bow, and another on starboard quarter. Decided best shot would be about 125 starboard track and maneuvered for this position. As this ship appeared loaded and was southbound, decided on a full salvo of six, depth setting 18 feet to minimize chances of prematures.

0106-00 Fired # 3 tube. 0106-12 Fired # 4 tube. 0106-22 Fired # 5 tube. 0106-31 Fired # 6 tube. 0106-50 Fired # 1 tube. 0106-55 Fired # 2 tube.

Started swinging left.

Could plainly see the tracks of four of the torpedoes. Three of them appeared to run under the target and expected to see some hits as TDC had been checking on during the entire run with radar ranges and TBT bearings. Spread was at least 150 percent of target length. At about this time target started tooting whistle rapidly to attract attention of escorts and fired bursts of 20 MM tracer firing not accurate and appeared to be toward opposite side of target. Shortly afterward the escort astern fired several shots from what sounded like a 3" gun, but firing was erratic and don't believe we were spotted.

records.title: Evasion of suspected ASW group

fields.event: Pinging still directly on us, could hear the echo from him. Rigged for silent running and went deep. Negative temperature gradient was indicated at 175 feet, ran at 200 feet, after we were below temperature gradient he apparently lost us, as he started searching with his sound gear. It is strongly suspected that this was an anti-submarine group for the following reasons: (a) Target had much shallower draft than his appearance would indicate. (b) Pinging came from the target, not from the escorts. (c) Puffs of smoke appeared to say 'come on'. (d) If we had been DF'd in our morning transmission he apparently had headed for the spot, instead of avoiding it.

records.title: Rendezvous with TUI and USS GROWLER

fields.event: Contacted and exchanged recognition signals with New Zealand corvette TUI (our escort) and USS GROWLER at Rendezvous, 5 miles west of CAPE ASTROLABE, MALAITA. Started proceeding on course 227 T, at 11 kts, leaving TULAGI, SAVO ISLAND and GUADALCANAL on the port hand and SANTA ISABEL on the starboard. During the day sighted many aircraft, mainly liberators and flying fortresses also sighted several patrol craft, several friendly DD's and many landing craft.
